inputs.original_text: This is being called “chaos,” but what stands out is a huge “No Kings” protest met with tear gas and arrests by federal officers. At least 13 arrests were confirmed in Portland and Denver. Labeling protesters “agitators” shifts attention away from the power imbalance: the state has force at its disposal, while people exercising their right to dissent face intimidation and arrest. A society that protects democratic rights should safeguard protest, not treat mass dissent as a threat to be suppressed.
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” protest is being presented as peaceful dissent met by state force, but that framing leaves out the basic responsibility of keeping public order. When a mass demonstration becomes chaotic, federal officers cannot simply stand aside; tear gas and arrests may be necessary to restore order. At least 13 arrests were confirmed in Portland and Denver. Grand slogans don’t place anyone above the rules or make every protester’s conduct beyond scrutiny. A free society protects dissent, but it also depends on respect for law and the institutions that hold it together.
